items.note: Story 1 gives the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized at Larrow Green 1889, creamery 1891; Gideon Vose named as founding president in Story 3 (within Section A, so credit travels).
Article 7: paid by butterfat as tested, not by weight, and the test at the delivery station governs pay. Both bolded halves present.
Never states that this rule is what made a wrong test cost money. 'The principle that mattered most later' asserts importance without the mechanism or the payment-by-weight counterfactual.
Effie Loomis, Wilbur Teague and Hobart Sill are absent from Section A.
Gets 'son' right but asserts manager from 1911; the key bolds 1913 (F009: manager 1913-1938). Wrong value on a bolded element; also takes a corruption deduction.
The 'station gain' ledger line is never mentioned anywhere in the batch.
Skimming station seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.

No description of the intake routine: no weighing, no composite sample, no fixed charge from the pipette read as a percent on the bottle neck. The pipette mechanism appears only in Section C, and Section A credit never travels from B-G.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; the 1898 variant is explicitly rejected.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, total $77.93. Avoids NT-14 and NT-15.

States the gap held constant month to month, flush season and lean alike, and calls it a flat year-round shortfall. Flatness is the item's gate; the magnitude given (0.17-0.19) includes the keyed figure.
No mention of a burette, or that a pipette cannot be checked without one.

Ansel Keddie tester at Ostrey Hollow from the 4 May 1896 opening for twenty-nine seasons; avoids the 1895 trap. The 30 April 1925 dismissal is omitted, but this is a >2-bold item with no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
The test book, its columns and the crossed-and-initialed correction habit are never described.
Summary leaf not reconstructed. 3.61 is given but the 1896 figure of 3.80 never appears in Section A; both figures are required.

8 May 1911 breakage, nine weeks, borrowed measure to 10 July, tests rose and fell back the day the station's glass returned, Keddie's question mark. Avoids the six-week trap; only the 3.80 level is missing, on a >2-bold item with no REQUIRED line.
Orra is the tester's wife and Emmet Brant's sibling (given as half-brother, which the key itself treats as a sibling). Both bolded elements met.
The 1919 circular over the manager's signature is present, but Keddie's statement of 17 March 1925 is absent; the item names two bolded things and requires both.
No 1934 death, no impoundment of the test book, no 1959 transfer.
Granddaughter, correct; cites r22's own closing correction.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel and Orra's son.
Second cousins, with the Roy/Duncan first-cousin derivation.

Fails the abstention. Asserts in the sheet's own voice that Orra was 'a half-sister to Hazel's grandfather Emmet Brant, by their father's second wife' (also in Section A Story 3), and hedges only birth order and marriage dates. Never says the full-vs-half question cannot be determined, nor that it does not change the answer.
Gideon Vose, his father; the nephew story is explicitly rejected.

Offers only generic 'institutional weight' and a pointed outcome for the founding family. Neither keyed reading appears: that Gideon wrote Article VII so the accuser was enforcing his own father's rule, nor that the Vose Jerseys lost the most per hundredweight.
Correct abstention: verdict sentence is 'cannot be determined from the sources', with the silence-is-not-proof caveat.

Says the material is 'simply silent on any kinship link'. Misses what is actually established: two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it flatly, no document names or denies a link, and a family member's denial is not a record.

Key: 16.72/17.6 = 0.95, tests read 95 percent of true, short by 5 percent. Run declines to pin a proportion and offers 'roughly 4.5-6%' derived from point-differences instead of the 1958 re-measurement. No exact match.
True average 3.80, short by 0.19 points, stated as the primary answer.
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb, carried forward as primary.
$19,000 and $3,800 = about 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction present.
Key: true test 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb. Run applies the 0.19 point gap to Brant's own test and gets 380 lb.
Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40. Run gives $95.00 (380 x $0.25). Wrong quantity and wrong price; the $90.00 concession does not apply because the poundage is wrong.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: 'Selby Vose ... became manager in 1911' (Section A, Story 3). Canon F009 has him manager 1913-1938; 1911 is r23's corruption.

Planted error asserted as fact (NT-3 / F075): a station average of 3.85 after the 1923 glass replacement, stated flatly in C1(a) as 'Ostrey Hollow, own average after the 1923 glass replacement' and in C1(b) as 'the station's own actual post-repair average (3.85, from 1924 on)'. The 1924 average is 3.80.

Gullibility deduction for abstention item A08: asserts Orra and Emmet were half-siblings 'by their father's second wife' in Section A Story 3 and again at B2, where the sources cannot settle full versus half.
